component.name: Unwall
component.summary: Control panel for the zapret/nfqws DPI bypass engine
zapret/nfqws DPI atlatma motoru için kontrol paneli

description.p: Unwall is a Linux control panel for zapret and zapret2, the DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) bypass engines by bol-van. It wraps the engine with a systemd service, nftables rules, encrypted DNS, gateway mode for consoles and smart TVs, and carrier presets, driven by a GTK4 interface that never runs as root.

Unwall, bol-van'ın DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) atlatma motorları zapret ve zapret2 için bir Linux kontrol panelidir. Motoru bir systemd servisi, nftables kuralları, şifreli DNS, konsol/TV için ağ geçidi modu ve operatör presetleriyle sarar; hiçbir zaman root olarak çalışmayan bir GTK4 arayüzü üzerinden yönetilir.

This package contains only the graphical interface. The privileged backend (unwallctl, the systemd unit and the nftables rules) must be installed separately on the host system — see the project README for native packages (Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/openSUSE) or the install script.

Bu paket yalnızca grafik arayüzü içerir. Yetki gerektiren arka uç (unwallctl, systemd birimi ve nftables kuralları) host sistemde ayrıca kurulu olmalıdır — native paketler (Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/openSUSE) ya da kurulum betiği için projenin README dosyasına bakın.

description.p: Unwall now measures instead of guessing. Auto-tune runs candidate strategies in a second engine on its own queue and scores them against sites that are actually blocked, without disturbing the connection you are using. A watchdog notices when a strategy stops working and can search for a new one on its own. Strategies are remembered per network, so home, a mobile hotspot and a school network each keep what works there.

A Wi-Fi hotspot mode lets a console or TV join a network broadcast by this machine instead of needing manual IP settings, and a new Health page collects the strategy check, the tuner, the network profile, the hotspot switch and the list counts in one place.

Measurement also learned to tell a block from everything else that can go wrong with a connection: a WebSocket endpoint answering HTTP 426, a live host with a mismatched certificate, or a name that simply no longer resolves are no longer mistaken for censorship, and "unwallctl prune" clears entries whose domain has gone away.

Auto-learned domains are now verified by measurement instead of being trusted. The engine's block detection is a guess - a site that is briefly down or a telemetry endpoint that never answers looks exactly like a blocked one - and on one real machine 368 of 497 learned entries had never been blocked at all. New learnings now land in a quarantine list and are promoted only once Unwall has opened two connections to the domain, one with the bypass and one without, and seen the difference for itself.

Adds "unwallctl verify" with an hourly timer and a button on the Lists page, the quarantine list in the interface, and a separate verdict for domains that are genuinely blocked but which the current strategy cannot beat.
The Status page fits in the window again and the Lists page is collapsible, capped and searchable instead of rendering hundreds of rows.
Added a connection test, a notification when a domain is auto-learned, a chooser for every working strategy blockcheck found, and a one-time note that closing the window does not stop protection.

Fixed gateway mode never actually redirecting the DNS queries of LAN devices (consoles, TVs): the rule only matched packets arriving on an interface other than the WAN one, which never happens on the usual single-NIC setup, and it pointed at systemd-resolved's 127.0.0.53 stub, which ignores queries coming from anywhere but the local machine. Queries are now matched by source address and sent to dnscrypt-proxy when DoH is on, or to a dedicated resolved listener on the LAN address otherwise.

Redirected queries were then dropped by ufw's default deny-incoming policy, since after redirection they are addressed to this machine and no longer covered by the forwarding rule; the matching allow rule is now added and removed along with gateway mode.
The Status page now shows your carrier without pressing a button, and reports encrypted DNS and gateway mode state at a glance.
Reorganised the interface into four pages — Status, Settings, Lists and Log — with an adaptive view switcher instead of one very long scrolling page.

Domains can now be added and removed straight from the new Lists page, and Unwall can detect your carrier from its ASN over encrypted DNS and pick the matching profile, optionally re-detecting when you move to another network.

Fixed hostlist-auto never being able to write autohostlist.txt or its debug log: without --user the engine dropped root to a fixed uid mapping to no real account. It now drops to "nobody" and the relevant files are chowned accordingly.

Fixed v1.3.14's ufw/firewalld gateway-forwarding fix silently failing under the service's ProtectSystem=strict sandbox (/etc/ufw and /etc/firewalld were read-only, so the rule never actually got added); failures are no longer silenced.

Fixed gateway mode devices getting "connected, no internet" when ufw/firewalld drop forwarded traffic by default. nft-apply now automatically adds a targeted ufw/firewalld forwarding rule for gateway mode and reverts it when gateway mode is turned off; unwallctl doctor / GUI Diagnostics show what was detected.

Fixed the gateway mode toggle logging a bare, confusing "=== gateway mode ===" line. Turned "How do I configure the device?" into a dedicated page with real Console/TV, Android and iPhone instructions showing the machine's actual gateway IP and subnet mask instead of generic placeholders.
Fixed hostlist mode dropdown values not being translated in Turkish (silently fell back to English).

Fixed "Restart now" after an in-app update sometimes reopening the old version: the restart now replaces the running process in place instead of racing a new one against the still-running old instance.
Fixed the About dialog showing a placeholder instead of real credits: it now shows the maintainer's name and a section crediting the upstream projects this port is based on.
Fixed the real cause of self-update's trailing "unbound variable" crash (a bash trap/set -u interaction, not file self-modification as first suspected); cleanup is now explicit.
hostlist-auto now learns a domain after a single genuinely failed connection attempt instead of requiring 3 within 60 seconds, so a second visit no longer needs a manual refresh.

Fixed install.sh corrupting a running self-update: the unwallctl script is now written to a temp file and renamed into place instead of being overwritten in place, so it can no longer read a mangled copy of its own currently-executing code.

Fixed hostlist-auto never learning genuinely blocked domains: the reply direction (incoming RST/redirect) is now queued too, as required by zapret2's own documentation, instead of only outgoing traffic.
Ask to restart after a self-update so the GUI picks up the new code; fixed a crash in the blockcheck confirmation dialog.
Made the "Update now" button work regardless of the currently installed unwallctl version (no longer depends on self-update already existing).
Added a self-update command and GUI button; fixed the update banner showing a stale version after several rapid releases.
Fixed a silent blockcheck failure, made encrypted DNS setup on Fedora reliable and censorship-resistant, fixed a cp warning.
Fixed a false DNS-poisoning positive, added a Fedora build dependency, and made gateway mode force LAN DNS through the local resolver.
Added AppImage packaging.
Fixed rpm spec macros, moved the Flatpak to a supported GNOME runtime, and fixed a false "not found" message in the Flatpak build.
Added .deb and .rpm packaging and a GUI-only Flatpak.
Licensed the project under GPLv3 and credited the author.
Initial release: Linux port with encrypted DNS, gateway mode and an English/Turkish GTK4 interface.
